must_identify.item: The container being killed is the log-shipper sidecar, not the api container
must_identify.evidence: The `api` application container in each pod remained healthy (Running, Ready: True, 0 restarts), while a second container, `log-shipper`, was repeatedly Terminated with Reason OOMKilled, Exit Code 137 [7].

must_identify.item: The sidecar is OOMKilled because its 16Mi limit is below its usage
must_identify.evidence: The `log-shipper` container's startup code immediately allocates a 40 MB in-memory buffer, as confirmed by its own log output ("buffering 40 MB before first flush") [12], against a configured container memory limit of only 16Mi [7]. This oversized allocation relative to the limit causes the kubelet to OOMKill the container on every start

notes: The fixes (raise the log-shipper memory limit, or roll back to revision 1) appear only in the Not Checked section and were not applied because of read-only policy. A reviewer should note the claim that a third pod remains on revision 1 at 1/1, which is plausible mid-rollout but goes beyond the scenario definition.
